text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Political differences can be successfully resolved within institutions which were created by the will of the people through political dialogue, says Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic.

- According to statistics, positive results in 1996 were GNP growth, increase in industrial output, maintenance of stable foreign exchange rate and low inflation; among negative results were a foreign trade deficit of two billion dollars.
- Serbian privatisation law to be put before parliament in spring 1997, says Serbian Deputy Prime Minister Svetozar Krstic.
- Serbian Parliament Speaker Dragan Tomic says parliamentary parties' panel discussion transmitted live will contribute to calming tensions present in the past weeks on the Serbian political scene.
- Serbian justice ministry declares incorrect a decision of Nis municipal electoral commission to repeat local elections in a number of electoral units.
- Privatisation in Yugoslavia could be carried out more easily than believed, says director of Belgrade economics institute Danko Djunic.
- Supporters of opposition coalition Zajedno continue protests over election results; police block marches through streets.

- Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic told Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic that Montenegrin parliament could Monday adopt resolution asking Serbian leadership to respect election results as recommended by OSCE.
- Serbian energy and mining minister Dragan Kostic says he expects stabilisation of power industry next year.
- Yugoslav agriculture minister Tihomir Vrebalov says 200 million dinars will be secured within coming 10 days to pay half of debt owed to farmers for purchased autumn crop.
- Serbian power industry calls consumers to cut down electricity consumption which has grown considerably due to cold weather.
